-10min ramp 50%->65% FTP (RPE 2-3)

sessions.description:
Off the bike. I want this week's work absorbed today, not added to.

Foam roll quads and glutes, eight to ten minutes. One long walk. Eat like you trained; a rest day is not a diet day.

If you feel great and want to ride, that is the point. Don't.
sessions.title: Rest Day

sessions.description:
Freshness is the work this week.

Light mobility only: hips, back, calves, ten minutes. A short walk. Feet up. Pack and check the bike today so nothing happens tomorrow.

No test efforts. No 'just checking the legs.'

FUEL:
Normal meal ~2h before. One bottle, 40-50g carbs. Done.

2min Killers — level 2

WARM-UP:
• 5min ramp 50%->70% FTP
• 6min @85%-91% FTP
• 3min @45%-55% FTP
• 3x 20s @125% FTP / 40s @45%-55%
• 2min @45%-55% FTP

MAIN SET:
-6x 2min @ 125% FTP (Z6, RPE 9-10, 90-100rpm) / 5min @ 45%-55% (Z1, RPE 1-2)

COOL-DOWN:
-10min spin-down 70%->50% FTP (RPE 2-3)

EXECUTION:
-Commit to each effort, rest fully between.

NUTRITION:
-40-60g carbs/hr.
sessions.pre_activity_comment:
Feels great? Extend the duration at the same power -- never add power.
Failed a set? Resume after 5-10min easy only if the early reps weren't already a struggle. Struggling from rep one: spin home easy and tell me.

sessions.title: Pre-Race Openers

sessions.description:
RACE DAY: Shawangunk Grit
Date: 2026-11-07

FUELING PLAN:
- Carbs/hour: 63g (range: [56, 70])
- Total carbs: 212g over race
- Start fueling at 20 min, every 20-30 min thereafter
- Pre-race: 100-150g carbs 3-4 hours before start

PACING STRATEGY:
- First 30 min: EASY. Let others burn matches -- I want you playing the long game.
- Mile 10-40: Find your rhythm. Target G SPOT zone (88-94% FTP) on climbs.
- Final third: this is where you pass people. Increase effort as others fade.
- Technical sections: Smooth > Fast. Avoid mechanicals.

HYDRATION:
- Drink to thirst — 500-750 ml/hr is a starting estimate to adjust for heat and sweat rate, not a quota. 500-1000 mg sodium per hour. Do not force fluid beyond thirst; you should finish a shade lighter than you started, never heavier.
